request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: suspended drop ceiling with metal grid and fissured acoustic tiles
floor-to-ceiling glazed ceramic wall tiles in a tiled enclosure
institutional-style tiled shower or wet-area enclosure

damaged_parts.condition: large brown irregular water stain with layered edges, cracked and flaking surface, dark spotting near the centre
dark discolouration along tile edges suggesting mould or dirt build-up

regional_indicators: drop ceiling with acoustic tiles and square ceramic wall tiles typical of North American commercial or institutional buildings
parsed_output.summary_en: A stained acoustic ceiling tile in a suspended grid ceiling shows a large brown water mark with layered edges, cracking and dark spotting, next to a tiled wall corner. The suspended ceiling and tiled enclosure suggest a commercial or institutional wet area rather than a typical private home, and the layered staining and dark spots indicate repeated or prolonged moisture.
